title: A Orchard for the Summer
premise: Marine biologist Emrys Reyes retreats to her late grandmother's coastal orchard for the summer, determined to inventory the land before selling it — until a freak spring storm strands her with Julian Voss, the rival scientist she loved and lost a decade ago, and his young daughter, Wren, who has never known a home. Forced to share the crumbling farmhouse, Emrys and Julian confront the misunderstanding that tore them apart while Wren quietly stitches them back together. When the orchard's fate is decided at auction, Emrys must choose between the secure career waiting across the country and the family standing in her doorway. She stays, they buy the orchard together, and love finally moves out of the past tense.
about_author: Rafael Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former tide-pool tour guide who traded salt water for storytelling and now writes romances set wherever the weather misbehaves. They live in a drafty coastal cottage with two cats named after failed expeditions.

chapters.title: The Trees Remember
chapters.summary: Emrys arrives at the overgrown orchard to catalog it for sale, armed with spreadsheets and old grief. A sudden storm knocks out the road, stranding her with Julian Voss — her former research partner and the man who broke her heart — and his quiet daughter Wren. POV: Emrys. Emotional beat: guarded resentment cracking into reluctant hospitality as three strangers share one dark house.

chapters.title: What the Storm Buried
chapters.summary: Powerless days force cooperation: pruning trees by daylight, playing cards by candlelight. Wren's questions about 'the lady from Papa's photographs' unearth the decade-old letter that never arrived — the misunderstanding that ended everything. POV: alternating Emrys and Julian. Emotional beat: rising tension as truth surfaces faster than either can forgive themselves for believing the worst.

chapters.title: First Fruit
chapters.summary: The auction notice arrives; the orchard sells in ten days. Emrys and Julian confess their regrets at last, and one kiss undoes years of careful distance — then panic: he's offered a post abroad, she's offered a lab across the country. POV: Emrys, closing on Wren's diary entry. Emotional beat: climax of love against duty, both choosing fear again until Wren runs away to the orchard's oldest tree, forcing them to choose each other instead.

chapters.title: A Season That Stays
chapters.summary: In the auction hall, Emrys outbids the developer with money she meant for a down payment; Julian matches it without hesitation, pooling their futures into one deed. They plant a new tree with Wren, whose adoption papers Emrys has begun filing. POV: Emrys, epilogue from Wren. Emotional beat: resolution — belonging chosen over safety, found family rooted where the storm began.
